facts.claim: UNESCO page 'Indonesian Batik' (state: Indonesia), inscribed 2009 on the Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity. Re-checked live: HTTP 200, title confirmed. Reused from indonesian-wedding-traditions pack fact_01.

UNESCO's description says special batik varieties are part of celebrations of marriage and pregnancy, and batik accompanies life from baby slings to funerary cloth; the element is tagged 'Wedding'. Page re-checked live (HTTP 200); claim carried from indonesian pack fact_02 (read in full 2026-11-03).

UNESCO describes batik made by drawing dots and lines of hot wax on cotton or silk, the wax resisting dye; the craft is often passed down within families. Page re-checked live; claim carried from indonesian pack fact_03.

ROYAL CONTEXT. Kraton Yogyakarta official page 'Dhaup Ageng' (16 April 2017, re-read live 2026-11-04, HTTP 200): Dhaup Ageng is the wedding a Sultan holds for his daughter; the page states that in Javanese tradition the wedding is held by the bride's side; the ceremony has been much simplified over time while keeping the core of each step.

ROYAL CONTEXT. Kraton Yogyakarta 'Dhaup Ageng': the sequence listed is lamaran, majang and pasang tarub, nyantri, siraman, tantingan, midodareni, akad nikah, panggih, tampa kaya, dhahar klimah, kirab, resepsi, pamitan. Useful as one documented order; not every family follows it.

ROYAL CONTEXT. Kraton Yogyakarta 'Dhaup Ageng', lamaran: once the couple agree to marry, the groom's side shows its seriousness through a lamaran (proposal) ceremony; after it is accepted, the wedding date and the steps and people involved are set. In the royal version the Sultan then gives both a new name and title.

ROYAL CONTEXT. Kraton Yogyakarta 'Dhaup Ageng', majang and pasang tarub: the point is to decorate the places where the ceremonies will happen and to ask that everything runs smoothly, marked with decorations and offerings; a bleketepe woven from young coconut leaf (janur) is put up on the roof; tarub (curved janur decoration) and tuwuhan (particular plants, leaves and seeds) are placed at several spots. On the palace page it is the event organisers who hang the bleketepe; the page does not say the bride's father does.
facts.conflicts: Brief expected 'put up by the bride's father'; the palace page names the event's officials for the royal wedding. Keep the father version as 'often told' unless batch sources confirm it.

facts.claim: ROYAL CONTEXT. Kraton Yogyakarta 'Dhaup Ageng', nyantri: a welcome for the groom-to-be and his family into the palace, framed as introducing him to the royal family's customs, rules and daily life; palace relatives collect them and bring them by horse carriage to the Kasatriyan (men's quarters), where they are hosted.

Kraton Yogyakarta 'Dhaup Ageng', siraman: the ritual bathing of both bride- and groom-to-be, meaning cleansing or purifying them outwardly and inwardly; done by the mother, the future mother-in-law and senior relatives of the bride as a blessing; bride and groom bathed at separate times and places, the bride first. (Re-check of indonesian pack fact_08.)

ROYAL PRACTICE ONLY. Kraton Yogyakarta: the bride-to-be is bathed with water from seven springs mixed with flowers; that water and the relatives who bathed her then go to the groom's siraman. Do not present seven springs as universal. (Re-check of indonesian pack fact_09.)

Kraton Yogyakarta: after siraman both are dressed and made up; for the bride this usually involves shaving (mengerik) the fine hairs on forehead and nape to form the outline (cengkorongan) of the paes ageng makeup. Supports ngerik in substance; 'juru paes' is not on the page. (Re-check of indonesian pack fact_10.)

Kraton Yogyakarta: midodareni is held on the night before the core wedding rites, as the bride's request that the next day goes smoothly; the name comes from 'bidadari' (heavenly nymph), a hope she will look as lovely as a nymph; nymphs are believed to descend near midnight; the custom is said to follow the Jaka Tarub story, who asked the nymph Nawangwulan to come down and make up their daughter Nawangsih the night before her wedding. Nothing on the page frames it as a hen or stag night. (Re-check of indonesian pack fact_11.)

ROYAL CONTEXT. Kraton Yogyakarta: akad nikah is the core rite that makes the couple husband and wife; the ijab qobul vow is spoken. In the palace it is held in Masjid Panepen, attended by men only, the Sultan himself marries off his daughter, and the groom then does sungkeman to the Sultan. (Re-check of indonesian pack fact_12, sungkeman detail added.)

Kraton Yogyakarta 'Upacara Daur Hidup Masyarakat Jawa' (7 August 2017; bibliography cites a 2009 Yogyakarta provincial culture office book): marriage is one of the three key life phases with birth and death; Javanese marriage has three big stages, pre-wedding, wedding and post-wedding; the page notes traditional ceremonies are being shortened or left out for cost or practicality, while the palace still holds them in full. Re-read live 2026-11-04, HTTP 200. (Re-check of indonesian pack fact_15.)

Official copy (BPK legal database, JDIH BPK) of Presidential Instruction No. 1 of 1991 on disseminating the Kompilasi Hukum Islam (KHI); re-checked live 2026-11-04, HTTP 200, title confirmed. The page holds the 2-page instruction only, not the KHI annex, so specific akad elements (wali, two witnesses, ijab kabul, mahar) are NOT confirmed from an official copy. (Re-check of indonesian pack fact_17.)

Kalurahan Girikerto (Sleman Regency village government site, culture data page 'Upacara Tradisi Daur Hidup dalam Fase pra-nikah, tahap pernikahan, dan tahap paska nikah'), read live 2026-11-04: nontoni is the first step toward marriage, a ceremony to see the prospective partner; lamaran comes second, after nontoni, once the young man accepts his parents' choice; if accepted, the bride's parents send an envoy with the answer (jawaban). Local village record (Sleman, Yogyakarta), not a statement for all Java.

Kalurahan Girikerto (Sleman) culture data page: peningsetan comes from 'singset', meaning to tie, so a peningset is 'a binder'; it is the fourth step, after the answer to the proposal is received. The page does not list the gift items.

Kalurahan Girikerto (Sleman) culture data page: putting up the tarub at the gateway of the bride-to-be's family home opens the series of ceremonies and also announces that the household is about to hold a wedding (hajatan mantu). Listed as 'Pasang tarub/Tuwuhan'.

Kalurahan Girikerto (Sleman) culture data page: nyantri means entrusting the groom-to-be to the bride's family for one to two days before the wedding; siraman is bathing the bride- or groom-to-be, meaning to cleanse oneself to become pure; adol dawet (selling dawet) follows the siraman.

Kalurahan Girikerto (Sleman) culture data page: midodareni is held between 6 pm and midnight; the bride- and groom-to-be must not sleep; it includes advice, counsel and prayers. Ijab qobul is the validation of the marriage according to the couple's religion; panggih brings bride and groom together as husband and wife after the religious and civil-registration steps; ngundhuh mantu is the final post-wedding step. The page also lists langkahan, done before the akad when a younger sibling marries before an unmarried older one.

ABSTRACT ONLY. Walisongo: Jurnal Penelitian Sosial Keagamaan 21(2) 2013, pp. 309-330, Waryunah Irmawati (IAIN Surakarta), 'Makna Simbolik Upacara Siraman Pengantin Adat Jawa', DOI 10.21580/ws.21.2.247: siraman is a Javanese ritual bathing held one day before the ijab qabul; its procedure and equipment (uborampe) are fixed (pakem) and carry symbolic meaning; the study links Javanese philosophy, culture and Islam. Abstract page read live 2026-11-04; full PDF not read.

ABSTRACT ONLY. Jurnal Sastra Indonesia (SASINDO) 11(1) 2022, Universitas Negeri Medan, Marlia, Harahap and Wuriyani, 'Makna Simbolik dalam Tradisi Peningsetan dan Pasang Tarub/Tratag dalam Pernikahan Adat Jawa', DOI 10.24114/sasindo.v11i1.36090: peningsetan is commonly called seserahan and has become a usual part of weddings in Indonesia, once not obligatory but now rooted; in the community studied, tarub/tratag is now used only at the kitchen area while the front uses wedding tents, and tarub decoration is replaced with plastic flowers; some objects and steps have been dropped as old-fashioned. Fieldwork setting (likely North Sumatra Javanese community) not confirmed from the abstract.

Widyaparwa 49(1) 2021 (peer-reviewed, Balai Bahasa DIY, Indonesian education ministry), Nardilla: a study of panyandra, the poetic narration by the master of ceremonies during panggih in the Surakarta style (Nganjuk, East Java), finding similes and metaphors of beauty, splendour and good wishes for the couple's household. Live re-check did not complete within the budget (fetch still running); claim carried from indonesian pack fact_16, read 2026-11-03. Treat as needing one re-check before publish.

insider_details.detail: Couples asking for 'the full set' should know the documented village sequence runs nontoni, lamaran, the formal answer, peningsetan, tarub, nyantri, siraman, adol dawet, midodareni, ijab, panggih and ngundhuh mantu, so pre-wedding customs can span weeks, not one weekend; ask each family which steps they keep.

Siraman is held the day before the ijab in the studied tradition and the palace bathes the bride first, then the groom elsewhere; for a destination wedding, plan two private bathing spaces and a gap in the run sheet so elders can move between them.

Midodareni runs from early evening to midnight with advice and prayers and the couple stay awake, so it is a quiet family evening, not a hen or buck's night; keep guest entertainment separate and avoid scheduling an early ceremony call the next morning without warning the families.

The tarub at the family gateway is a public signal that a wedding is coming; at a hired venue, agree early where the janur and plant decorations will go and who installs them, since many families now use tents and simplified decorations.
Palace details such as seven-spring water, a men-only akad in the palace mosque and the Sultan conducting the vow are royal practice; brief vendors and guests that ordinary family weddings differ.
